summary: The product catalog service pod kill exposed a single‑replica failure that caused checkout to fail with a 51.6% error rate and 60 s latency spikes. A network partition of the payment service did not raise error rates but produced a 17 s p95 latency spike, indicating a slowdown rather than a service outage. A 30% packet loss to the currency service pushed p95 latency to 2.8 s, again a slowdown without data loss.

findings.title: Product catalog pod kill causes checkout failure
findings.what_happened: Killing the sole productcatalogservice pod caused checkout and product pages to return 500 errors, raising error_rate to 0.516 and p95 latency to 60 000 ms.
findings.root_cause: The service ran with replicas=1 and no PDB, so the pod kill removed the only instance, breaking all downstream calls.
evidence: frontend: {"error":"could not retrieve product: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = \"transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 10.96.223.78:3550: connect: connection refused\""

findings.title: Payment service network partition causes latency spike
findings.what_happened: A network partition between paymentservice and checkoutservice caused checkout to experience a 17 s p95 latency spike, though error_rate remained 0.0.
findings.root_cause: The fault isolated paymentservice from checkoutservice, delaying payment processing but not causing errors.
findings.fix: No fix applied; consider adding a retry or circuit breaker for paymentservice calls.

findings.title: Currency service 30% packet loss causes latency spike
findings.what_happened: A 30% packet loss to currencyservice increased checkout p95 latency to 2.8 s, exceeding the 1 s baseline, but error_rate stayed at 0.0.
findings.root_cause: Network loss degraded communication with currencyservice, slowing price conversion calls.
findings.fix: No fix applied; consider improving network reliability or adding retries for currencyservice calls.
